questions.question: What is the capital expenditure (CAPEX) allocated for Indian Railways in the financial year 2024-25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.62 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **capital expenditure (CAPEX) allocated for Indian Railways** in the financial year 2024-25 has been set at ₹2.62 lakh crore.
 
• This allocation marks a **significant increase** compared to previous years, underlining the government's focus on infrastructure development.
 
• It is the **highest-ever CAPEX allocation** for Indian Railways, aimed at modernizing and expanding railway infrastructure.
 
• The funds will be utilized for projects such as **track doubling, electrification, station redevelopment, and rolling stock acquisition**.
 
• Emphasis has also been placed on **high-speed rail projects** and improving passenger amenities across the railway network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Expenditure (CAPEX):**

 
 
• CAPEX refers to funds used by an organization or government to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets like infrastructure, buildings, or equipment.
 
• In the context of Indian Railways, it includes investments in projects like electrification, new lines, and station redevelopment.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways Modernization:**
 
 
• The modernization plan includes electrification of routes, the introduction of semi-high-speed and high-speed trains, and enhanced safety measures.
 
• It also focuses on automation and the use of technology to improve operational efficiency.
 
 
 
• **High-Speed Rail Projects:**
 
 
• India's flagship high-speed rail project is the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor.
 
• Such projects are expected to reduce travel time and boost regional economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Green Initiatives:**
 
 
• Indian Railways aims to achieve **net-zero carbon emissions by 2030**, with a focus on renewable energy and electrification of rail routes.
 
• Large-scale solar and wind energy projects are being integrated into railway operations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Increased CAPEX:**
 
 
• Higher CAPEX in railways is expected to boost employment, regional connectivity, and economic growth.
 
• It is also likely to improve logistics efficiency, reducing costs for businesses and consumers.

questions.question: What was the theme of the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) Convention held in January 2025?

options.text: Redefining Engagement with the Indian Diaspora
Strengthening Bonds: The Indian Diaspora and India@75
Engaging Diaspora for a Self-Reliant India
Diaspora's contribution to a Viksit Bharat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diaspora's contribution to a Viksit Bharat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The theme of the **18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** (PBD) Convention held in January 2025 was **"Diaspora's contribution to a Viksit Bharat."**
 
• The event was organized by the Government of India to celebrate the contributions of the Indian diaspora in the country’s development journey.
 
• A "**Viksit Bharat**" refers to the vision of a **developed India**, aligning with the nation’s goals for **2047**, marking 100 years of independence.
 
• The PBD convention serves as a platform for the Indian diaspora to engage in discussions about India’s progress and their role in nation-building.
 
• The event highlighted the importance of the diaspora’s expertise, innovation, and investments in building a strong and self-reliant India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD):**

 
 
• PBD is celebrated on** January 9 **every two years to honor the contribution of the overseas Indian community towards India’s development.
 
• The date commemorates Mahatma Gandhi's return to India from South Africa on January 9, 1915.
 
• The convention facilitates networking opportunities for the diaspora to interact with Indian leaders and policymakers.
 
 
 
• **Viksit Bharat Vision 2047:**
 
 
• It is a roadmap envisioned by the Indian government to transform India into a developed nation by 2047, marking the centenary of independence.
 
• The focus areas include economic growth, social equity, technological advancements, and sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Indian Diaspora:**
 
 
• The Indian diaspora, one of the largest in the world, comprises over 32 million Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs).
 
• They play a crucial role in fostering bilateral relations, economic contributions, and cultural exchanges between India and their respective countries of residence.
 
 
 
• **Role of Diaspora in India’s Development:**
 
 
• They contribute through remittances, investments, and knowledge transfer in various sectors such as IT, healthcare, and education.
 
• Indian-origin leaders and professionals around the world enhance India’s global stature and influence.

questions.question: What is the target number of houses to be built under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) by 2023-2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.89 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban), the government aims to provide housing for all by 2023-2024, targeting the construction of **1.89 crore houses**.
 
• The scheme was launched on **25 June 2015** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, focusing on urban areas.
 
• The initiative aims to address the housing shortage among the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Low-Income Groups (LIG), and Middle-Income Groups (MIG).
 
• PMAY (Urban) includes four verticals: In-situ Slum Redevelopment, Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), and Beneficiary-led Construction (BLC).
 
• By the end of 2022, **over 1.22 crore houses had been sanctioned**, with significant progress in construction and occupancy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**

 
 
• It is divided into two categories: **PMAY (Urban)** for urban areas and **PMAY (Gramin)** for rural areas.
 
• The scheme aims to achieve "Housing for All" by providing affordable housing to urban poor and rural populations.
 
• Beneficiaries under PMAY are selected based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data.
 
 
 
• **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS)**
 
 
• Under PMAY (Urban), CLSS provides interest subsidies on home loans for beneficiaries in EWS, LIG, and MIG categories.
 
• The subsidy varies based on income groups, with interest rates ranging from **6.5% to 4% annually**.
 
 
 
• **Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP)**
 
 
• Encourages partnerships between public and private sectors to construct affordable housing projects.
 
• Central assistance of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per house is provided for eligible beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Beneficiary-led Construction (BLC)**
 
 
• Under BLC, financial assistance is provided to beneficiaries to build or enhance their own houses.
 
• Beneficiaries receive **up to Rs. 1.5 lakh** for constructing houses on their own land.

questions.question: According to the Future of Jobs Report 2025, which of the following is identified as the most transformative trend for businesses by 2030?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Broadening digital access**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Future of Jobs Report 2025** by the World Economic Forum highlights "Broadening digital access" as a transformative trend for businesses by 2030.
 
• This trend refers to ensuring that **digital connectivity and technology** are accessible to underserved populations and regions.
 
• It emphasizes the role of digital inclusion in reducing inequalities and fostering economic growth globally.
 
• With a focus on equitable access, broadening digital access addresses **digital literacy, infrastructure, and affordability** challenges.
 
• Governments, private sectors, and international organizations are collaborating to **bridge the digital divide** and enable global participation in the digital economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Divide:** The gap between individuals and communities with access to digital technologies and those without. It is a critical barrier to global economic and social equity.
 
• **Digital Literacy:** The ability to use digital tools and technologies effectively. Digital literacy is essential for participating in the modern economy and accessing essential services.
 
• **Global Connectivity Initiatives:** Programs like *Starlink* (by SpaceX) and *Project Loon* (by Alphabet) aim to provide internet connectivity to remote and underserved regions.
 
• **Impact of Digital Inclusion:** Increasing access to digital technologies can improve education, healthcare, financial inclusion, and entrepreneurship opportunities worldwide.
 
• **Role of 5G Technology:** 5G networks are expected to play a major role in enhancing digital access by providing faster, more reliable internet to more people.

questions.question: PM Modi's visit to which country in November 2024 marked the first by an Indian Prime Minister in 17 years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nigeria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• PM Narendra Modi's visit to Nigeria in November 2024 marked the first by an Indian Prime Minister since Manmohan Singh’s visit in 2007.
 
• The visit aimed to strengthen bilateral relations, focusing on areas such as trade, energy, defense, and cultural exchange.
 
• Nigeria is India's largest trading partner in Africa, and the two countries share strong economic ties, particularly in the oil and gas sector.
 
• The visit included discussions on enhancing cooperation in renewable energy, counterterrorism, and technology sharing.
 
• PM Modi participated in high-level meetings with Nigerian leaders and attended events celebrating India-Nigeria diplomatic ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nigeria-India Bilateral Relations:**

 
 
• Nigeria is among India’s top oil suppliers, accounting for a significant share of crude oil imports.
 
• India is one of Nigeria’s largest trading partners, with trade volumes exceeding $14 billion annually.
 
• Over 50,000 Indians reside in Nigeria, contributing to sectors such as healthcare, education, and technology.
 
 
 
• **India-Africa Relations:**
 
 
• India has consistently engaged with African nations through the India-Africa Forum Summit, focusing on development and capacity building.
 
• Key areas of cooperation include agriculture, healthcare, education, technology, and sustainable development.
 
• India’s lines of credit and grants have financed various infrastructure and development projects across Africa.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Nigeria:**
 
 
• Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country and boasts one of the continent’s largest economies.
 
• Its geopolitical influence in West Africa makes it a key partner for India in regional and global affairs.
 
• Counterterrorism and regional stability are shared priorities for India and Nigeria.
 
 
 
• **Historical Ties:**
 
 
• India and Nigeria established diplomatic relations shortly after Nigeria’s independence in 1960.
 
• Both nations are members of the Commonwealth and share a legacy of colonial history.
 
• Cultural exchanges, including Bollywood’s popularity in Nigeria, have strengthened people-to-people ties.

questions.question: In 2025, which Indian state initiated scientific coal mining after a decade-long ban on unscientific mining practices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meghalaya resumed scientific coal mining in 2025 after a decade-long ban on unscientific and hazardous mining practices, particularly rat-hole mining.
 
• The ban was initially imposed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) in 2014 due to severe environmental degradation and safety concerns caused by unregulated mining activities.
 
• The resumption followed the introduction of stricter regulatory frameworks and environmental safeguards to ensure sustainable mining practices.
 
• Scientific mining involves the use of advanced technologies and practices to minimize environmental impact and enhance worker safety.
 
• This move was seen as a significant step toward balancing economic development and environmental conservation in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rat-Hole Mining:**

 
 
• A method of coal mining involving narrow and shallow tunnels, often criticized for its hazardous working conditions and environmental impact.
 
• This practice was prevalent in Meghalaya, leading to the NGT ban in 2014.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT):**
 
 
• A specialized judicial body in India established in 2010 for the effective and expeditious disposal of environmental cases.
 
• It plays a crucial role in enforcing environmental laws and addressing ecological concerns.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Mining:**
 
 
• A modern and regulated approach to mining that minimizes environmental impact and ensures safety through the use of advanced technology.
 
• It includes measures such as controlled blasting, proper waste management, and land reclamation.
 
 
 
• **Coal Mining in Meghalaya:**
 
 
• Coal is a major resource in Meghalaya, contributing to the state's economy and employment.
 
• The transition to scientific mining is expected to boost economic development while preserving the ecological balance.

questions.question: In March 2025, the Indian government sought parliamentary approval for additional spending. Which sector was allocated funds for upgrading networks in underserved areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telecommunications**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In March 2025, the Indian government allocated additional funds to **upgrade telecommunications networks** in underserved and remote areas.
 
• The focus of this funding was to **bridge the digital divide** by expanding internet and mobile connectivity in rural and tribal regions.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s **Digital India mission**, which aims to transform the country into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• The investment was directed toward improving **fiber-optic infrastructure and mobile tower installations** in geographically challenging areas.
 
• The telecommunications sector plays a critical role in enabling access to **e-governance, education, healthcare, and financial inclusion** services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital India Program:**

 
 
• Launched in 2015, it aims to provide **universal digital connectivity** and governance through technology.
 
• Key initiatives under this program include **BharatNet**, which focuses on connecting gram panchayats with high-speed internet.
 
• The program also promotes digital literacy through schemes like **PMGDISHA (Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan)**.
 
 
 
• **BharatNet Project:**
 
 
• An ambitious initiative to provide **broadband connectivity to 2.5 lakh gram panchayats** across India.
 
• It is implemented in phases and aims to ensure high-speed internet reaches the grassroots level.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Telecommunications in Rural Areas:**
 
 
• Telecommunications act as a **backbone for e-learning, telemedicine, and e-commerce** in remote regions.
 
• Improved connectivity fosters **economic development** by enabling entrepreneurship and job creation.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Expanding Telecom Infrastructure:**
 
 
• Geographical barriers like mountains and dense forests make installation costly and time-consuming.
 
• Lack of reliable power supply in rural areas hinders the operation of telecom equipment.
 
 
 
• **Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF):**
 
 
• Established to provide financial support for **telecom services in rural and underserved areas**.
 
• Funds are collected from a Universal Service Levy imposed on telecom operators.

questions.question: India’s first indigenous CAR-T therapy and gene therapy for Hemophilia, discussed during the 7th PM-STIAC meeting in January 2025, were presented by experts from which institutions?

options.text: IIT Bombay and St. John’s Hospital, Bengaluru

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Bombay and St. John's Hospital, Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India's first indigenous CAR-T cell therapy** was developed collaboratively by **IIT Bombay** and **St. John's Hospital, Bengaluru**.
 
• The CAR-T (Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell) therapy is a cutting-edge treatment for cancer that uses engineered T-cells to target and destroy cancer cells.
 
• The gene therapy for Hemophilia discussed at the **7th PM-STIAC meeting** was also presented by experts from IIT Bombay and St. John's Hospital.
 
• The PM-STIAC (Prime Minister's Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council) meeting serves as a platform for discussing breakthroughs in science and technology.
 
• The development of indigenous CAR-T therapy and gene therapy is a significant step in reducing dependency on costly international treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CAR-T Therapy:**

 
 
• CAR-T therapy is a revolutionary form of immunotherapy where T-cells are genetically modified to express chimeric antigen receptors.
 
• It has shown remarkable results in treating blood cancers such as leukemia and lymphoma.
 
• Globally, CAR-T therapies are expensive, costing millions, making indigenous development crucial for accessibility.
 
 
 
• **Gene Therapy for Hemophilia:**
 
 
• Gene therapy for Hemophilia involves delivering functional copies of genes responsible for producing clotting factors.
 
• Hemophilia is a genetic disorder that impairs the blood's ability to clot, leading to excessive bleeding.
 
• Advancements in gene therapy aim to provide long-term solutions by addressing the root genetic cause.
 
 
 
• **PM-STIAC:**
 
 
• The **Prime Minister's Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council **(PM-STIAC) advises the government on science, technology, and innovation strategies.
 
• It facilitates collaborations between government agencies, researchers, and institutions to drive advancements.
 
• The council focuses on leveraging science and technology for societal and economic benefits.
 
 
 
• **IIT Bombay's Role in Biotech:**
 
 
• IIT Bombay has been at the forefront of research in biotechnology and healthcare solutions.
 
• Its collaboration with St. John's Hospital highlights the importance of academia-industry partnerships in healthcare innovation.

questions.question: Who will be the first Indian astronaut to travel to the International Space Station (ISS) as part of Axiom Mission 4?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shubhanshu Shukla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shubhanshu Shukla is set to become the first Indian astronaut to travel to the International Space Station (ISS) as part of the **Axiom Mission 4**.
 
• Axiom Mission 4 is a private crewed mission organized by **Axiom Space** in partnership with NASA.
 
• This groundbreaking mission will mark India's entry into human space exploration beyond Earth orbit in collaboration with international partners.
 
• The mission is part of Axiom Space’s efforts to expand commercial space exploration and pave the way for private astronauts to conduct scientific research in microgravity.
 
• Shubhanshu Shukla’s selection highlights India’s growing presence and contributions to global space exploration initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Space Station (ISS)**

 
 
• The ISS is a multinational collaborative project involving NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), and CSA (Canada).
 
• It serves as a microgravity and space environment research laboratory where scientific studies are conducted in various fields, including biology, physics, and astronomy.
 
• The ISS operates at an altitude of approximately 400 km and travels at a speed of 28,000 km/h.
 
 
 
• **Axiom Space**
 
 
• Axiom Space is a private American aerospace company focused on commercial space missions and building the first commercial space station.
 
• The company organizes private crewed missions to the ISS, offering opportunities for research, education, and commercial activities.
 
 
 
• **India’s Space Program**
 
 
• India's space program is spearheaded by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), which has achieved significant milestones in satellite launches, lunar exploration, and interplanetary missions.
 
• Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight program, aiming to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit by 2024.
 
 
 
• **Microgravity Research**
 
 
• Microgravity refers to the condition in which objects appear weightless due to the free-fall motion of the spacecraft.
 
• Research in microgravity allows scientists to study phenomena that are not observable under Earth’s gravity, such as fluid dynamics, material science, and biological processes.

questions.question: On 26 March 2025, where was the 8th State Level Coordination Committee (SLCC) meeting conducted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gangtok**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **8th State Level Coordination Committee (SLCC) meeting** was conducted by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** on **26 March 2025** in **Gangtok, Sikkim**.
 
• SLCC meetings are held to review and coordinate measures for combating illegal deposit-taking activities in the respective states.
 
• The event involves participation from **state government officials, regulators, and law enforcement agencies**.
 
• Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim, hosted the meeting to address state-specific financial and regulatory concerns.
 
• The SLCC serves as a key platform to enhance inter-agency coordination and protect the public from fraudulent financial schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Level Coordination Committee (SLCC)**

 
 
• SLCC is an inter-regulatory body chaired by the RBI, established to address **unauthorized deposit activities** in states.
 
• The committee includes representatives from SEBI, IRDAI, state governments, and law enforcement agencies.
 
• It monitors entities involved in potentially illegal financial activities and facilitates timely action.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI in Financial Regulation**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank responsible for **monetary policy, financial stability, and supervision of banks** in India.
 
• It also safeguards consumers by combating fraudulent schemes through regulatory measures and public awareness campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Gangtok - Key Highlights**
 
 
• Gangtok is the capital city of Sikkim, a northeastern state in India known for its picturesque landscapes and cultural heritage.
 
• It serves as a hub for governance, tourism, and regional development activities in the state.
 
• Gangtok is also an important venue for hosting government and regulatory meetings due to its strategic location.
 
 
 
• **Public Awareness Initiatives**
 
 
• RBI conducts various initiatives to educate the public about **fraudulent financial schemes** and encourages reporting suspicious activities.
 
• Awareness campaigns through media and public outreach programs are crucial in combating illegal deposit collection.

questions.question: Which of the following actors was honoured with the 2025 International Goya Award for his contributions to global cinema?
questions.solution:

• He has also been recognized for his humanitarian work, including advocacy for human rights, environmental conservation, and Tibetan causes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Established in 1987, the Goya Awards celebrate excellence in Spanish cinema.
 
• They are organized by the Spanish Academy of Cinematic Art and Sciences.
 
• The ceremony includes categories such as Best Film, Best Director, and Best Actor.
 
• International awards recognize contributions to cinema beyond Spanish borders.
 
 
 
• **Richard Gere's Humanitarian Work:**
 
 
• Gere is a prominent advocate for Tibetan independence and a supporter of the Dalai Lama.
 
• He is involved in various charities, including HIV/AIDS awareness and environmental protection.
 
• He founded the Gere Foundation to support humanitarian causes globally.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact of Cinema:**
 
 
• Cinema serves as a powerful medium to influence culture, society, and global awareness.
 
• International awards like the Goya recognize the transnational impact of film and its creators.
 
• Richard Gere’s career exemplifies how cinema can bridge cultural divides and inspire audiences worldwide.

questions.question: Who were the winners of the Balbir Singh Sr Award for Player of the Year 2025 in the men’s and women’s categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harmanpreet Singh and Savita Punia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Harmanpreet Singh**, captain of the Indian men's hockey team, was awarded the Balbir Singh Sr Award for Player of the Year 2025 in the men's category.
 
• **Savita Punia**, captain of the Indian women's hockey team, received the same award in the women's category for her exceptional performance.
 
• The awards are named after **Balbir Singh Sr**, one of the greatest hockey players in Indian history and a three-time Olympic gold medalist (1948, 1952, and 1956).
 
• The award recognizes outstanding contributions to Indian hockey and aims to inspire players to excel in their performances.
 
• Harmanpreet Singh and Savita Punia were acknowledged for their leadership, consistency, and significant contributions to India's success in international hockey tournaments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harmanpreet Singh**

 
 
• Harmanpreet Singh is renowned for his expertise in drag flicks and is one of the top scorers in international hockey.
 
• Under his leadership, the Indian men's hockey team achieved significant milestones, including a bronze medal at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021.
 
• He was also named the FIH Men's Player of the Year in 2021 and 2022.
 
 
 
• **Savita Punia**
 
 
• Savita Punia is often referred to as the "Wall of Indian Hockey" due to her exceptional goalkeeping skills.
 
• She played a key role in India's historic fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, where the women's team reached the semifinals for the first time.
 
• Savita has been instrumental in India's victories in tournaments like the Asian Champions Trophy and the Commonwealth Games.
 
 
 
• **Balbir Singh Sr**
 
 
• Balbir Singh Sr was an iconic figure in Indian hockey, celebrated for his unmatched skills and sportsmanship.
 
• He holds the record for the most goals scored in an Olympic men's hockey final, with five goals in the 1952 Helsinki Olympics.
 
• In 2012, he was named one of the 16 greatest Olympians of all time by the International Olympic Committee (IOC).
 
 
 
• **FIH Awards**
 
 
• The International Hockey Federation (FIH) recognizes outstanding players, goalkeepers, and coaches annually through the FIH Hockey Stars Awards.
 
• India has frequently dominated the awards in recent years, reflecting the country's resurgence in global hockey.

questions.question: According to luxury resort developer Fine Acers 2025, the market for branded residences and resorts in India is expected to reach ₹8,610 crore (US$ 1 billion) by

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• These are luxury residential properties developed in collaboration with globally recognized hospitality or lifestyle brands.

questions.question: According to the Economic Survey 2025, what was the unemployment rate in India for 2023-24?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **According to the Economic Survey 2025**, the **unemployment rate **in India for the financial year** 2023-24 **was recorded at **3.2%**.

• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):** Provides guaranteed wage employment to rural households.
 
• **Start-Up India:** Encourages entrepreneurship and innovation to generate employment.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten indicators used in calculating the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Internet connectivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is calculated using ten indicators across three broad dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• The indicators under the health dimension include **nutrition** and **child mortality**.
 
• Under the education dimension, the indicators used are **years of schooling** and **school attendance**.
 
• The standard of living dimension includes indicators such as **access to electricity**, drinking water, sanitation, cooking fuel, housing, and asset ownership.
 
• **Internet connectivity** is not one of the indicators used in calculating the MPI, as it focuses on basic needs and capabilities rather than technological access.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• Developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• Aims to provide a more comprehensive measure of poverty beyond just income levels.
 
• It captures the overlapping deprivations individuals or households face across multiple dimensions.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions and Indicators:**
 
 
• Health: Nutrition, Child Mortality.
 
• Education: Years of Schooling, School Attendance.
 
• Standard of Living: Cooking Fuel, Sanitation, Drinking Water, Electricity, Housing, Assets.
 
 
 
• **Global MPI Reports:**
 
 
• The MPI is included in the **Human Development Reports** released annually by the UNDP.
 
• It provides valuable insights into poverty trends and is used for policymaking and international comparisons.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Basic Needs:**
 
 
• The MPI emphasizes fundamental human needs such as health, education, and basic living standards.
 
• Technological access, including internet connectivity, is not included as it is not considered a core indicator of poverty reduction.

questions.question: What is India’s renewable energy target by the year 2030 in terms of installed capacity?

• LPSC is one of ISRO's key centers, responsible for developing liquid propulsion systems for launch vehicles and spacecraft.
 
• It plays a critical role in missions such as PSLV, GSLV, and cryogenic engine development.
 
 
 
• **ISRO's Major Missions:**
 
 
• **Gaganyaan:** India's first human spaceflight mission, aiming to send astronauts to space by 2026 and 2027.
 
• **Chandrayaan-3:** A lunar exploration mission focused on soft-landing technology.
 
• **Mangalyaan-2:** The second Mars mission to further study the Martian atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Future Vision:**
 
 
• ISRO is expanding international collaborations and private-sector involvement in space technology.
 
• It aims to strengthen India's position in satellite launches, interplanetary exploration, and space-based applications for societal benefits.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the Olympic Order by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in July 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhinav Bindra**__.

__
 
• **Abhinav Bindra**, India's **first individual Olympic gold medalist**, was awarded the **prestigious Olympic Order by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in July 2024**.
 
• The Olympic Order is the highest honor granted by the IOC, recognizing individuals for their exceptional contributions to the Olympic Movement and sports.
 
• Bindra won the gold medal in the **10m Air Rifle event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics**, marking a historic achievement for India.
 
• He has been actively promoting sports development and athletes' welfare through initiatives like the Abhinav Bindra Foundation.
 
• The award celebrates his enduring impact on Indian sports and his contributions to Olympic values and excellence.

• **Olympic Order:**

 
 
• The Olympic Order is awarded to individuals who demonstrate outstanding merit in the development of sport and uphold the Olympic ideals.
 
• It is symbolized by a chain and badge, with the five Olympic rings representing global unity through sports.
 
 
 
• **Abhinav Bindra’s Contributions:**
 
 
• Bindra has contributed significantly to sports science and athlete preparation in India through his foundation.
 
• His autobiography, "A Shot at History," details his journey to Olympic glory and inspires young athletes worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Indian Sports Achievements:**
 
 
• India has consistently improved its Olympic performance, with notable contributions from athletes like Neeraj Chopra and PV Sindhu.
 
• Bindra's 2008 gold medal paved the way for greater focus on individual sports in the country.
 
 
 
• **IOC and Its Role:**
 
 
• The International Olympic Committee oversees the organization of the Olympic Games and promotes global sports development.
 
• The IOC recognizes individuals and organizations that align with its vision of promoting peace and unity through sports.

questions.question: Who among the following won the 2024 Booker Prize, and what is the title of the winning novel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samantha Harvey – Orbital**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Samantha Harvey** is the winner of the 2024 Booker Prize for her novel **Orbital**.
 
• The Booker Prize is one of the most prestigious awards in literary fiction, recognizing outstanding novels written in English.
 
• **Orbital** explores themes of existentialism, human connection, and the vastness of the cosmos, receiving critical acclaim for its innovative narrative style.
 
• Samantha Harvey is a well-known British author whose previous works have also been shortlisted for various literary prizes, including the Orange Prize and the Costa Book Awards.
 
• The announcement of the Booker Prize winner took place at a grand ceremony held in London in 2024.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Booker Prize Overview:**

 
 
• Established in 1969, the Booker Prize is awarded annually for the best novel written in English and published in the UK or Ireland.
 
• The prize aims to celebrate literary excellence and promote the global recognition of English-language novels.
 
• The winner receives £50,000 along with a significant boost in book sales and international recognition.
 
• Authors from any nationality are eligible as long as their work meets the language and publication criteria.
 
 
 
• **Samantha Harvey's Literary Contributions:**
 
 
• She is known for her deep philosophical insights and experimental narrative structures.
 
• Her previous novels include "The Wilderness," "All Is Song," and "Dear Thief," which have received critical acclaim.
 
• Her works often delve into complex human emotions and existential themes.
 
• Harvey’s literary style is characterized by lyrical prose and profound storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Key Themes in Orbital:**
 
 
• The novel examines human curiosity and our place in the universe.
 
• It intertwines individual struggles with broader cosmic questions.
 
• Orbital has been praised for its intellectual depth and emotional resonance.
 
• It challenges readers to reflect on the meaning of existence and the interconnectedness of life.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Booker Prize:**
 
 
• Winning the Booker Prize significantly enhances an author's career and global reach.
 
• The recognition often leads to translations into multiple languages and adaptations into other media formats.
 
• The prize has historically boosted the visibility of literary fiction and brought attention to emerging and established authors alike.
 
• It serves as a benchmark for literary quality and innovation in storytelling.

questions.question: According to the Economic Survey 2023-24, how many Indians are estimated to have escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.5 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Economic Survey 2023-24 highlighted that **13.5 crore Indians escaped multidimensional poverty** between 2015-16 and 2019-21.
 
• This significant reduction was attributed to the government’s **focus on inclusive growth and targeted welfare programs.**
 
• **Multidimensional poverty** considers multiple deprivations, such as health, education, and living standards, beyond monetary poverty.
 
• India demonstrated remarkable progress in poverty reduction, aligning with its Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
 
• The report utilized data from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) and **UNDP's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• A measure developed by the UNDP and Oxford Poverty & Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• It assesses poverty beyond income, focusing on **deprivations in health, education, and living standards.**
 
• Indicators include nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, access to clean water, electricity, and housing.
 
 
 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS):**
 
 
• A large-scale, multi-round survey conducted in India by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• NFHS provides data on population, health, and nutrition trends across states and the country.
 
• It is a crucial resource for policymaking and tracking progress on poverty alleviation.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Adopted by the United Nations in 2015, SDGs consist of **17 global goals aimed at ending poverty, reducing inequality, and tackling climate change by 2030.**
 
• India’s efforts to reduce multidimensional poverty align with SDG 1: No Poverty.
 
 
 
• **Government Welfare Programs:**
 
 
• Several schemes such as Ayushman Bharat, PM-KISAN, and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana contributed to poverty reduction.
 
• Focus on **housing, healthcare, education, and financial inclusion** has improved living standards for millions.
